beats.speaker: speaker
beats.text: Bright One forgive me. Forty years I lit that round, and the Council gave it to nobody. The factor wants his coin by the new moon. A flask here, a flask there. They'd have gone dark anyway.

scenes.title: A name for the Chapel roll

beats.speaker: priest
beats.text: Every name the tide took is owed a candle. This one waited twenty winters. Keep yours lit on Restday, between the bells, and I'll read his name so he can hear it.

scenes.title: At the door of Grayrock Hall

beats.speaker: speaker
beats.text: A rope order with our seal on it. Twenty winters late, and still ours. Grayrock pays what it owes. Tell the brother a widow's due will come down from the Hall.

scenes.title: The coal crier in the Rag Market

beats.speaker: speaker
beats.text: A farthing a sack, and folk still haggle. A lighter brings it off the pier foot, wet from the bilge. I grew up by the clamps. I know wet coal. I sold it anyway.

beats.speaker: speaker
beats.text: It's only one loaf. Gran's on short days at the yard. The chute's just my size. And I leave a coal on the step for it. That makes it a trade.

quests.title: The Dark Round
quests.summary: The Sump lamps run dry by midnight, and the Lamp Store blames the Lamp and Wick's oil. Walk the lamplighters' round after dusk, find where the oil goes, and decide what the oil-seller is told.

offer.ask: You look worn down to the wick.
offer.say: #greet#. The Lamp Store buys our oil for the Sump lamps, and since the old lamplighter lost his round they run dry by midnight. They say our oil's thin. It isn't. Walk the round after dusk: Net Court, the Pawn corner, the Knucklebones steps. Two flasks. Keep your nose open.
offer.accept: I'll walk your round after dark.
offer.handIn: The round's walked. I know where the oil went.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A lamp's a small thing until it's out. The Lamp Store will hear our oil was never thin, and I'll count you with the honest ones. It's not a long list.

quests.title: The Grey Paw at the Cinder Gate
quests.summary: Night wagons leave the Cinder Gate with a grey paw on the tally and no customs seal. Keep the gate with its guard after dark, follow the ruts, and bring back the tally.

offer.say: #greet#. Quiet's the word for it. Wagons go out of my gate after dark with a grey paw on the tally and no customs seal, and they come back light. I can't leave the gate. You could. Keep it with me after dusk, then follow the ruts.
offer.accept: I'll keep the gate with you, then follow them.
offer.handIn: The tally's where I said it would go.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Grey paw on a board. You'd think they'd be ashamed to sign it. Mind the south road.

quests.title: What the Wharf Owes
quests.summary: Twenty winters ago a Grayrock crane let go over the north pier and a wharf hand drowned under the load. Find the truth on paper for his brother, then choose what the truth is for.

offer.ask: You remember every debt, they say.
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Twenty winters ago a Grayrock crane let go over the north pier, and my brother went under the load. The Wharf Office wrote 'the river took him.' The river never tied a knot in its life. Find me the truth on paper, would you? Before I'm too old to care.
offer.decline: Some things are better left in the water.
offer.handIn: It's done, the way you wanted.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Twenty winters I've carried that. It's lighter in somebody else's paws for a day. Sit, there's soup on.

objectives.label: Ask a Records Office clerk to look out the old wharf rolls. The clerks drink at the Grey Gull after work.

See it done.

quests.title: Down the Sunken Street
quests.summary: The butcher's boy and the baker's little one went down the Sunken Street steps hunting ghosts, and the Chapel bells have rung twice since. Bring them up.

offer.say: #greet#. My boy and the baker's little one went down the Sunken Street steps after lessons, hunting ghosts. The Chapel bells have rung twice since, and they're not up. I can't leave the block with meat out. Please. Bring them up.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Oh, #thanks#. Look at the state of them. I counted every bell, you know. Every one.

quests.title: Smoke over Northgate
quests.summary: Somebody cries wet coal door to door in Northgate at a farthing a sack, and chimneys are catching. Find the seller, find where the coal comes ashore, and decide whether the Watch hears of it.

offer.say: #greet#. It does, and it shouldn't. Somebody's crying coal door to door at a farthing a sack. Wet slack. It smoulders in the flue till the soot catches. The flat over the Grey Goose went up last night. Find me the seller? Then we'll decide who hears of it.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. I'll write it in the book: who, where, and what it cost. I write everything down. It's the only way a thing stays true.

quests.title: The Cooper's Note
quests.summary: The cooper's father paid the Counting House, every penny, and their book says otherwise. The note falls due by the new moon. Pay it, or prove it.

offer.ask: You look like a wolf counting days.
offer.say: #greet#. My father borrowed from the Counting House, and paid it, every penny. He told me so at the end, and he never lied to me. Their book says otherwise, and the note's due by the new moon. I can't call a House a liar on my own. Will you help me settle it, one way or the other?
offer.accept: One way or the other, it'll be settled.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Here, a cask, a good one, with your mark burned in the lid. It's what I can spare, and it'll outlast us both.

objectives.label: Decide: raise the coin, or find the proof.
Win a pot at the Knucklebones.
Give the cooper twenty pennies for the note.

quests.title: The Short Larder
quests.summary: The servants' hall larder at Timberland Court comes up a loaf short every morning. Sit up by the old coal chute after the house is dark, follow what you find home, and decide what the Court is told.

offer.ask: You look like a wolf who's counted something twice.
offer.say: #greet#. Twice, and short both times. One loaf gone from the hall larder every morning, and a heel of cheese. The other servant says rats. Rats don't take exactly one loaf. The old coal chute comes out back here. Sit up by it after the house is dark? Find who comes, before the steward does.
offer.accept: I'll sit up by the chute.
offer.handIn: I know where your loaves go.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. I keep coal in my pocket for luck, you know. Born in the Sump. Funny what you can't put down.
